messages:
maria: Heads up — got a latency-burn-rate alert for /v1/generate in us-west-2 at ~07:02 PST. Seeing token-level SLO burn even though p99 request latency looks okay in the high-level dashboard. I'm starting a quick trace.

devon: ack. Can you dump a few traces? curious if it's KV cache misses or kernel selection thrashing.

maria: Pasted one trace snippet from the per-token breakdown:
```
token_idx=0   fetch_kv=12ms  kernel_pick=matmul_opt(0)  compute=4ms  serialize=1ms
token_idx=1   fetch_kv=95ms  kernel_pick=matmul_opt(1)  compute=3ms  serialize=1ms
token_idx=2   fetch_kv=110ms kernel_pick=matmul_opt(1)  compute=3ms  serialize=1ms
...
summary: kv_miss_spike between tokens 1-3, kernel selection flip from matmul_opt(0) -> matmul_opt(1) under long-seq path
```

priyanka: that kv fetch jump is concerning. Any correlation with batching size changes? We had the autoscaler bumping batch window at 07:00.

maria: yes — noticed batching heuristic adjusted max_batch=64 -> 128 for that pod group around the alert. When batch doubled, the runtime started preferring the alternate kernel for longer sequences; seems kernel_latency variance + KV lock contention caused token-level latency spikes.

sam: rough root cause hypothesis: batching heuristic increased max_batch which changed sequence-length distribution across workers, triggering kernel selection policy to pick a kernel variant that is fast for large dense batches but suffers when KV cache misses cause memory stalls. So p50 unaffected, p95 okay sometimes, but token-level SLO burns.

devon: makes sense. Any profiler flamegraphs?

maria: uploaded a short perf dump to the perf dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dash/perf/trace/1742109987 — key callouts: 40% CPU wait on kv-io, kernel-switch overhead 7% per-token during the spike, and context-switch stalls when batch size >96.

perf-bot: ALERT: latency-burn-rate fired for route /v1/generate (us-west-2) — burn rate 0.35 over 5m window (threshold 0.2). Incident created: INC-2026-213.

priyanka: Proposed mitigations: 1) temporarily cap max_batch to 96 for affected ASGs; 2) add a short-circuit in kernel selection to prefer the low-variance kernel when KV miss rate > 10%; 3) tighten burn-rate alarm to 0.18 for critical routes. Thoughts?

sam: +1 for short-term cap. We should be careful about throughput tradeoffs. For kernel selection change, can we gate by a runtime flag (no rollout) and A/B only on a small ASG?

devon: I'll open a quick PR to add a runtime flag + metric export for kernel_choice and kv_miss_rate per-pod. Need those metrics in the token-level breakdown panel so we can alert on kernel churn.

maria: I've started a canary rollback plan: flip batching heuristic back at 07:15 for the two ASGs that hit >10% burn. Rolling now — patching config via /ops apply.

ops-bot: deploy request accepted — applying batching config patch to asg-gen-usw2-1, asg-gen-usw2-2.

maria: After the cap we saw immediate drop in kv fetch variance and burn-rate returned to 0.06 in 8m. p99 tail still slightly elevated but under paging threshold.

priyanka: For longer-term: add instrumentation to dashboards: per-route token-level breakdowns should include kernel_choice histogram, kv_miss_rate (per-token window), and batch_size_distribution. Also add an alert composer that can fire on kernel_churn_rate > X and kv_miss_rate delta > Y.

sam: Also recommend adding an anomaly detector on token-latency z-score over a 30-day baseline (not just burn rate). That would catch rare regression patterns we miss today.

devon: Action items I captured:
- PR: export kernel_choice + kv_miss_rate per pod (devon)
- Dashboard: add 3 panels to /dash/perf/routes (priyanka)
- Playbook: update paging thresholds for token-burn to 0.25 -> 0.2 and add kernel-churn alert (maria)
- Run a small AB test for kernel short-circuiting (sam)

maria: I'm adding the playbook note now. Also adding an entry to postmortems if we don't already have one for kernel churn as a perf regression vector.

priyanka: small note — when you cap max_batch, watch unit-cost. We may see cost per token go up briefly. Worth notifying sales/finance if the cap lasts >2h.

maria: good call. I'll notify ops and finance if we keep cap >2h. For now we revert to normal config after 45m and will monitor.

devon: Thanks — closing the incident once the burn-rate stays <0.1 for 30m across both ASGs.

maria: closing update: burn-rate stable at 0.04 for 35m, kernel_choice churn down to baseline. Leaving the runtime flag in staging for AB tests. Will follow up with a short writeup in #eng-runtime later. :white_check_mark:
